source.original_title: 05/14/2026 - Prem Patel & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/14/2026 - Prem Patel & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Lost

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'you spoke with kim i think right yeah yeah he gave me uh like a head start on you anyway'. Nothing specific from her notes was reflected back.

prospect.name: Prem Patel
prospect.location: Brooklyn, New York City, USA — works in Manhattan
prospect.occupation: Works for Meta in New York and is simultaneously founding his own company, into which he is putting significant personal capital. Describes himself as 'a numbers guy, a business guy'.
prospect.training_background: Highly active and long-trained. Plays tennis roughly twice a week, does a 20-mile cycle once a week and rides everywhere, rock climbs at a bouldering gym in New York, and lifts. Has worked with personal trainers for a long period and had good results, but is moving away from machines toward natural movement. Has an Equinox membership at about $200 a month. Trialled Trevor's kettlebell workouts at the gym for a couple of weeks before booking the call and reported strong results — new soreness, a visible pump, a sense of getting bigger. Used a 12 kg bell in those sessions and could not complete the third round of a set. Self-describes as under 10% body fat with visible abs.
prospect.medical: Volunteered an autoimmune condition and nothing further was established: 'so I have an autoimmune condition, so I'm really dialed into my eating.' The condition was not named, its severity was not established, no medication or treatment was mentioned, and no clinician was referenced. The rep did not acknowledge or ask about it at any point, moving directly to protein arithmetic. Gluten-free. No injuries disclosed.

signals: The purest good-to-great framing in the batch: 'I've just been in this zone for so long that I'm like, I need to get in a good program and get to the next level'
Already fit and successful — sub-10% body fat, visible abs, tennis, cycling, rock climbing, and a Meta job plus a company he is founding

Wants quality over cheapness and says so: 'I could go on ChatGPT or something, create me a kettlebell workout, whatever. But I kind of want to work with something that has been vetted and works before for people'
Forward-looking rather than remedial: 'I'm also trying to bulletproof the body... when I'm 60, 70, I'm trying to be running, biking, playing tennis'

Tension worth recording: price was a hard barrier here, not a quality signal — 'I won't be doing that' the moment $6,000 was quoted — which is bargain-hunter behaviour. Assigned optimizer because the constraint is situational, capital committed to a startup, rather than dispositional, and because he did buy the $200 product without hesitation.

Secondary read of skeptical_bargain_hunter is defensible: he is self-directed, self-accountable, did his own vetting before the call, and is anchored to free Trevor content that was already producing results

goals.text: Get to a stable 140 lb from 130 — add size, not lose it
Get out of a plateau he has been stuck in for years and reach a visibly different level
Build bigger arms, shoulders, back and legs — the parts he says he has neglected
Perform better at tennis and cycle faster
Bulletproof the body so that at 60 and 70 he is still running, biking and playing tennis
Move to natural movement patterns and away from machines
Get a properly structured, vetted programme rather than inventing his own or generating one from ChatGPT
Be able to train at home without needing the gym

pains.text: Plateaued for years despite consistent training — 'I feel like I've just been staying in the same area'
Has never had a good programme and does not know how kettlebell progression works — asked directly whether it is progressive overload, different movements, or beginner-to-advanced
Discovered gaps in his own training after trying Trevor's workouts: 'I have not been working on that part of the back, even though I've been going to the gym'
Struggles to hit protein targets, which he believes is what blocks the size gain
An autoimmune condition that keeps him tightly constrained on food
Previously avoided cardio and circuits for fear of burning calories he needed to gain weight, and it was not working
Only knows how to train in long gym sessions
Capital committed to a company he is starting, so discretionary spending is constrained

objections.raw_quote: Yeah. Yeah. I won't be doing that, but I'm open to hearing if there's different options in terms of like, um, you said there's, it's, it can be built around on a specific, like what you need, right? Like if I don't need 24 seven, if I don't need X, Y, Z, like, is it flexible in that case?
objections.rep_response: Refused to unbundle, correctly and on a stated reason: 'We don't want to take, cause like, we guarantee the results. And if we start taking things out, like the support, it kind of takes away from our success rate.' He then listed the other terms — three months at 4K and the year at 9K — rather than isolating the objection.

objections.raw_quote: The only concern I have, not concern is like, I don't know how intensive I need right now... I don't know if I need, like, for example, the 24-7 Trevor thing. I don't know how many questions I would actually ask. The check-ins are great. The adaptability is great.
objections.rep_response: Reframed 24/7 access as front-loaded into the first month for form correction — 'the 24-7 is most important in the first month, just while the form's tweaking. When you train, just record it, send it to Trevor.' The prospect softened: 'Okay. All right. Let's, yeah, I'm hesitant, but you know what? It's only a beneficial thing.'

objections.raw_quote: the only reason why I wouldn't do the training is one, like, I am working, I do work for Meta here in New York, but I also am starting a company and I'm putting a lot of money into it. So I don't really want to spend the 6k.
objections.rep_response: Offered a tax write-off — 'You can write it off as tax as well for your future' — which the prospect rejected outright ('That doesn't do anything for me. It's still money out the door'). The rep answered 'Fair' and continued demonstrating the $200 self-guided product. No financial-picture questions were asked and no payment plan was mentioned until a vague aside at the end of the call.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Mentioned only as an undeveloped aside after the sale was lost: 'if you're like, hell yeah, I want to take it even further. Let me know. Cause we can break it down.' No terms, no numbers, no follow-up.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'in six months, we guarantee that from your starting weight, you will put on eight kilo of your kettlebell on every lift... if you're doing that with a 12 kilo, you're basically doubling the weight, and it's like, you double the weight that you're doing it with, with the same intensity, the same reps, like your body is going to change... If you do everything we say, you don't get that within the six months, then we'll just work with you until you are at that.' Also used as the reason the bundle cannot be broken up.

prospect_financials.note: No financial-picture questions were asked. Volunteered: employed at Meta with a concurrent startup absorbing personal capital, currently paying roughly $200 a month for an Equinox membership, and explicitly unwilling rather than unable — 'If there was unlimited funds, I would absolutely do this training... I just can't spend the 6K on it right now.'

evidence: Explicit and immediate no to the coaching on hearing the price: 'Yeah. Yeah. I won't be doing that'

Restated at the end with a reason: 'If there was unlimited funds, I would absolutely do this training. Like to work with Trevor, that guy's ripped... There'd be absolutely guaranteed I'd get bigger from it. I just can't spend the 6K on it right now.'
The rep pre-emptively argued against the coaching before quoting: 'Before I get into it, like what I would say to you is that you don't need to do the coaching'

Converted instead to the $200/month self-guided Primal University product, with two links sent by text and the prospect confirming intent — 'I'll do this man' and 'excited to be part of the community'
No coaching payment, no coaching link, no deposit and no follow-up call booked

Counter-evidence that this was winnable: he had already trialled the workouts and loved them, said the coaching would 'absolutely guaranteed' work, and described his own preferred path — start on a guide, then upgrade — which nobody diarised or structured
outcome.next_step: Prospect to sign up independently for Primal University at roughly $200/month via two links texted during the call, and to buy 12, 16 and 20 kg kettlebells on the rep's recommendation. No follow-up call booked and no upgrade path diarised, despite the prospect describing exactly that path unprompted.

notable.note: Three things. First, the prospect volunteered an autoimmune condition at 00:16:23 and it was never acknowledged — the rep went straight to protein grams and later prescribed specific bell weights, without a single question about what the condition is, whether it is treated, or whether anyone has cleared him. Second, this is the third call in the batch where the rep talked a prospect out of the $6,000 coaching and into the $200 self-guided product, and here he said the quiet part aloud: 'I'm in sales, I find it hard to upsell people out of this.' He also recited the ICP definition at the prospect, using the acronym. Third, the prospect described the exact commercial pathway the business appears not to have — 'I would like to start with like a Trevor guide, try it out for a month, two months, and then be like, hey, this is awesome, I'm realizing I have some spots here that I need help, I think the coaching could take me to the next level. That's how I usually start these kinds of things' — and nothing was set up to capture that upgrade. He also rejected the tax write-off pitch flatly, the second time that pitch appears in two days.

quality.notes: Severe and near-total inversion for long stretches. The opening block to 00:01:08 is attributed entirely to the rep but contains both sides including the prospect's question about the live-stream notice. From 00:03:16 to 00:05:07 the labels alternate incorrectly — 'I love that, man' is the rep under a Harry label but the following prospect speech is also under Harry. The entire price exchange at 00:23:13-00:24:42 is inverted, with 'For six months. It's six grand' labelled Prem. The Primal University walkthrough from 00:28:05 onward mixes both speakers under single labels with no boundaries. Every attribution in this file was resolved from content.
